media/audio-reactive.notes:
The effects are classes (`m-ar-pulse`, `m-ar-glow`, `m-ar-ring`, `m-ar-bounce`) that read the default names; put one on
any child of the wrapper too. `--m-ar-k` is the strength, `--m-ar-c` the color.
media/audio-reactive.a11y:
- It is decoration: the wrapper adds no role. Give it one (and a name) when the motion means something, or say it in
  text nearby ("Ada is speaking").
- Reduced motion: the source reads twice a second; pulse and bounce stop changing size and place, light and color
  still follow. `motion={false}` keeps everything still.

media/carousel.notes:
```tsx
<Carousel perView={2} m:color="brand-orange" prevIcon={arrowLeft} nextIcon={arrowRight} labels={{ previous: "Earlier", next: "Later", slide: (n) => `Photo ${n}` }}>{slides}</Carousel>
<Carousel dots={(i) => i + 1} arrows={false} smooth={false}>{slides}</Carousel>
```
media/carousel.a11y:
A labelled `section` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`. The track is focusable (arrow keys scroll it); the
previous / next buttons and the dots are labelled buttons ("Previous", "Next", "Slide n", translated); the active dot
is marked. The buttons sit at the inline edges and mirror in right-to-left layouts.

media/corner-mark.a11y:
Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`): say what it means in the name of the tile ("Video: …"). With `label` it is
`role="img"` with that name. It never takes pointer events, so the card under it stays clickable. `show="hover"` also
shows on keyboard focus and is always visible on touch screens; reduced motion: no slide.

Images take `alt` (empty: decorative); video and audio keep native controls (keyboard and screen reader friendly).
A failed load is announced as a status message. Images load lazily and decode off the main thread.

media/overlay.a11y:
Decorative by default: `aria-hidden`, inert, no pointer events (clicks reach the content underneath). Video and
canvas pause off screen and stay still with reduced motion; the canvas loop runs on the motion engine's clock
("pause all" and the global speed reach it). Position and size are CSS variables set through CSSOM (CSP safe).

media/spectrum.a11y:
- The spectrum is an image (`role="img"`) named "<label>: <level in words>, loudest near <frequency>" (for example
  "Spectrum: loud, loudest near 220 Hz"); it changes at most once a second. With no signal it says "No signal".
- Quiet bars are drawn dimmer as well as shorter, so the shape does not depend on color alone.
- Reduced motion: no falling caps, and the source reads twice a second. Off screen it does not draw at all.

Class hooks: `m-wave`, `m-wave-track`, `m-wave-canvas`, `m-wave-playhead`, `m-wave-regions`, `m-wave-region`,
`m-wave-marks`, `m-wave-mark`, `m-wave-bars`; CSS variables `--m-wave-h`, `--m-wave-bw`, `--m-wave-gap`, `--m-wave-bar`,
`--m-wave-played`; `data-state` is `loading`, `ready`, `error` or `live`.
media/waveform.a11y:
- Seekable: `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow` in whole seconds (percent without a duration) and `aria-valuetext`
  "1:05 of 4:00, Chapter 2", so the spoken value changes at most once a second while it plays. Arrow keys mirror in RTL.
- Not seekable: `role="img"` named "<label>, <duration>". Decorative bars are hidden from screen readers.
- The bars, regions and playhead mirror on right-to-left pages. Reduced motion: no grow-in, the decorative bars stand
  still, a live source updates twice a second.
